name: Algonquin Tiverton Lateral
monitor_reason: length: the project adds almost no new pipe, so it fails the 25 km new-pipe rule
researcher_notes: The Energy Information Administration lists a completed lateral called Algonquin Tiverton Electric Expansion, 16 miles of 30 inch pipe, in service April 2000, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket CP99-46 (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 150, August 2026 release, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx). The Federal Register notice of 25 January 1999 for the same docket describes something different. The project raised the pressure rating of about 20 miles of the existing Algonquin main line from 750 to 900 psig between Burrillville, Rhode Island and Mendon, Massachusetts. It replaced about 2.3 miles of existing pipe in short sections, built one new 545 foot 10 inch tie-in and a meter station at the Tiverton power plant, and raised the horsepower of two turbines at the Chaplin compressor station in Connecticut. It added up to 46,000 dekatherms per day of service to Tiverton Power Associates. So the 16 miles is mostly existing main line that was uprated, not a new lateral. New pipe is well under 1 mile, far below the 25 km floor. No separate row is justified. The existing Algonquin main line row (P0149) is the home for this capacity work. Not found: any source stating 16 miles of newly built pipe.
